rule: "SME" covers micro, small and medium businesses. Banks must use the headcount and turnover thresholds in Federal Cabinet Resolution No. 22 of 2016 (or later amendments).
citation: CBUAE Circular 1/2021, Art. 1 (definitions)

rule: Trading: < 5 employees or < AED 3m revenue. Manufacturing: < 9 employees or < AED 3m. Services: < 5 employees or < AED 2m.
citation: CBUAE Circular 1/2021, Art. 1, quoting Cabinet Res. 22/2016

rule: Trading: 6–50 employees or < AED 50m. Manufacturing: 10–100 employees or < AED 50m. Services: 6–50 employees or < AED 20m.
citation: as above

rule: Trading: 51–200 employees or < AED 250m. Manufacturing: 101–250 employees or < AED 250m. Services: 51–200 employees or < AED 200m.
citation: as above

rule: SME Customer Protection Regulation, Circular 2/2026, issued 17 Feb 2026, in force about Sept 2026 (six months after Official Gazette publication). It replaces the 2021 SME Market Conduct Regulation. It covers all CBUAE-licensed banks and finance companies, conventional and Islamic.
citation: CMS (10 Apr 2026); Pinsent Masons (2 Apr 2026). Verify exact in-force date on rulebook.

rule: Lender must assess affordability before giving credit. The 2021 rule (Art. 4.2) said: do not give credit beyond what the customer can service.
citation: Pinsent Masons on C 2/2026; Circular 1/2021 Art. 4.2

rule: Fees must not exceed CBUAE maximum fee limits. No fee for original paper statements. No closing or penalty fee if the account has been open more than 6 months.
citation: CMS on C 2/2026

rule: At least 60 calendar days' written notice before changes to terms (including fees). Auto-renewal needs a new 30-day notice.
citation: CMS on C 2/2026

rule: Lender must tell the applicant the reason for rejection, except for financial-crime reasons or where law forbids.
citation: Circular 1/2021 Art. 2.5. Verify it is carried into C 2/2026.

rule: No credit granted or extended without the customer's express, documented prior request.
citation: Circular 1/2021 Art. 4.3 (verify carry-over)

rule: Lender must help proactively after the first missed payments. It must have a framework for restructuring and adjusted payment plans. Arrears contacts must be proportionate and kept on record for 5 years after settlement or write-off.
citation: CMS on C 2/2026

rule: Lenders are encouraged to link to credit guarantee schemes, the movable collateral registry and SME credit scoring services.
citation: Circular 1/2021 Art. 3.6

parameter: "Adequate guarantees" for individuals and sole proprietorships
rule: Article 150 of Federal Decree-Law No. 6 of 2025 (new Central Bank law): lenders must obtain and keep adequate guarantees for all credit to natural persons and sole proprietorships, sized to income and facility amount. CBUAE sets the criteria. If not met, courts may dismiss the bank's claim.
citation: Tamimi; Paul Hastings; court reports (secondary). Verify against the Gazette text.

rule: CBUAE Circular 3/2023 (under old Art. 121 bis): a bare personal guarantee is not enough security for a facility. It must come with securities in rem (security over assets).
citation: Mondaq / BSA (May 2023). Verify status under the 2025 law.

rule: Emirates Development Bank Credit Guarantee Scheme with partner banks. At 2019 launch: up to 85% guarantee on loans up to AED 2m to start-ups. Later bank MoUs (Emirates NBD, ADCB, Emirates Islamic): up to 50% of the facility.
citation: EDB press releases; Khaleej Times; Gulf News. Verify current terms on edb.gov.ae (page did not load).

rule: Joint scheme from mid-2024. Combined cover up to 80% of the loan amount, shared between EDB, ECI and the partner bank.
citation: eci.gov.ae and edb.gov.ae news (Jun 2024)

rule: 75% risk weight for exposures that meet "regulatory retail" criteria (natural persons and SMEs). Value cap: total exposure to one SME counterparty ≤ AED 4,000,000. Granularity: no single counterparty > 0.20% of the retail portfolio.
citation: CBUAE Capital Adequacy Standards (C 52/2017, STA, as effective 1 Dec 2022), via rulebook search snippet. Page itself blocked (403). Verify.

parameter: Unrated SME that fails retail criteria
rule: 85% risk weight.
citation: as above (search snippet). Verify.

rule: From 2 Jan 2022, under Federal Decree-Law 14/2020 (amending the Commercial Transactions Law): a cheque returned for insufficient funds is no longer a crime in most cases. Crime stays only for bad faith and other cheque offences.
citation: CBUAE press release, 1 Nov 2021

rule: The drawee bank must pay whatever balance is available if it is less than the cheque value, unless the holder refuses. The holder can pursue the rest through execution.
citation: CBUAE press release, 1 Nov 2021; now in Decree-Law 50/2022 (Commercial Transactions Law), Art. 648 per Legal500

rule: The holder of a bounced cheque can go directly to the execution judge (the cheque is an enforceable instrument). The police complaint route is not needed.
citation: Legal500 / Chambers secondary (2025). Verify article numbers.

rule: Federal Decree-Law No. 51 of 2023 on Financial Restructuring and Bankruptcy. Gazetted 31 Oct 2023, in force 1 May 2024. Replaces Decree-Law 9/2016. Sets up a specialised Bankruptcy Court. Director liability extends to managers and de facto managers. A debtor in cessation of payments must file within 30 working days.
citation: Akin Gump; Dechert; Al Tamimi (secondary)

rule: No single "SME lending" definition. Companies Act size bands (meet 2 of 3), for periods starting on/after 6 Apr 2025. Micro: turnover ≤ £1m, balance sheet ≤ £500k, ≤ 10 staff. Small: ≤ £15m, ≤ £7.5m, ≤ 50 staff. Medium: ≤ £54m, ≤ £27m, ≤ 250 staff. No sector split.
citation: gov.uk "Life of a company: accounts"; SI 2024/1303

rule: The FCA regulates business lending only inside the consumer credit perimeter. In practice that means loans of £25,000 or less to sole traders and small partnerships. Lending to limited companies, and business lending above £25,000, is outside FCA remit.
citation: FCA press release 17 Sep 2026 (FS26/2); RAO Art. 60C (business-purpose exemption). Verify the "2 or 3 partners" detail in the RAO text.

rule: FS26/2 (17 Sep 2026): regulation "not a major obstacle". No change to the £25,000 perimeter. Next steps: Consumer Credit Act reform (HMT), open finance with SME lending as a priority use case, digital verification.
citation: FCA press release 17 Sep 2026

rule: The LSB closed at end Oct 2025 after a solvent wind-down announced 25 Jun 2025. Its Standards of Lending Practice for business customers (SMEs up to £25m turnover) are **no longer independently overseen**. Some banks say they still follow them voluntarily. No successor body named.
citation: LSB "The LSB's Legacy" (30 Oct 2025); Danske Bank UK notice

rule: Statutory scheme (live 1 Nov 2016). 9 designated banks must offer to refer SMEs they decline to designated finance platforms (with consent). HMT response, May 2026: leave the BRS law unchanged for now and seek industry-led improvements. 132,636 referrals up to Q1 2026.
citation: HMT Government Response, May 2026; BRS Official Statistics, Jul 2026

rule: Designated banks must share SME credit data with designated credit reference agencies. Turnover threshold £25m kept. HMT plans (when Parliament allows) to designate non-bank lenders, add business deposit data, and get consent from SMEs outside the scheme.
citation: HMT Government Response, May 2026

rule: 70% government guarantee to the lender on the outstanding balance. Borrower stays 100% liable. Max £2m per business group. Products: term loans, overdrafts, asset finance, invoice finance, asset-based lending. Business must be viable and not in difficulty.
citation: gov.uk scheme page (29 Jun 2026); gov.uk news (13 Jul 2026)

rule: Turnover cap raised from £45m to £54m. Max term from 6 to 10 years for loans up to £1.1m (above £1.1m stays 6 years). Capacity +£2bn/year by 2028/29. Go-live of these changes: "coming weeks" (not confirmed).
citation: gov.uk news 13 Jul 2026; Simply Business 22 Jul 2026

rule: Official 2026 pages give no end date. One trade source says support continues "until 2030".
citation: gov.uk; FF News. Unconfirmed.

rule: Lenders cannot take the borrower's principal private residence (main home) as security under GGS. Personal guarantees are allowed at any facility size if normal lender practice.
citation: British Business Bank GGS FAQ (search snippet; page 403)

rule: No statutory cap. The LSB had required annual checks on guarantees and clearer guarantor communications (Sept 2024 Standards). With the LSB closed, this is voluntary only. Most personal guarantees sit on limited-company lending, outside the FCA perimeter.
citation: LSB (Sept 2024 Standards); FCA FSB super-complaint follow-up page

rule: PRA PS1/26 (20 Jan 2026): Basel 3.1 takes effect **1 Jan 2027**.
citation: Bank of England PS1/26

rule: Removed from Pillar 1 from 1 Jan 2027. A firm-specific Pillar 2A "SME lending adjustment" is meant to stop overall SME capital going up.
citation: PS1/26 para 1.16; PRA PS7/25 (via search)

rule: 85% for unrated corporate SME exposures that are not retail. 75% for qualifying retail SME exposures kept.
citation: PS1/26 para 2.6 (85%); 75% from secondary summaries. Verify the retail SME exposure limit in the PRA Rulebook.

rule: SBA size standards by industry (NAICS code), either average annual receipts or number of employees, set in 13 CFR 121.201. Applicant plus affiliates are counted. There is no single national number.
Gross annual revenue of **$1 million or less** in the preceding fiscal year (down from $5m in the 2023 rule).
citation: CFPB 2026 final rule, per law-firm summaries

rule: None in general. TILA and most consumer rules do not apply to business-purpose credit. ECOA / Regulation B **does** apply (anti-discrimination and adverse action notices).
citation: 12 CFR 1002 (eCFR)

rule: Notice within 30 days of a completed application. May be oral or written. If the applicant asks for reasons within 60 days, the lender must give them within 30 days.
Notice "within a reasonable time", oral or written. Written reasons only if requested in writing within 60 days.

Revised final rule issued 1 May 2026. Effective about 30 Jun 2026. **Single compliance date: 1 Jan 2028.** Applies to lenders with ≥ 1,000 covered small-business originations in each of the two prior years (was 100). Excludes merchant cash advances, agricultural loans and loans ≤ $1,000. The old tiered 2026–2027 dates are replaced.
citation: CFPB final rule via Husch Blackwell / Mayer Brown / Steptoe summaries (search). Verify against Federal Register.

rule: About 10–11 states (CA, NY, UT, VA, FL, GA, KS, MO, CT, TX, plus LA per some). CA applies to deals up to $500k; NY up to $2.5m. Banks are commonly exempt (for example CT), but not in all states (LA has no exemptions). Texas HB 700 (2025) covers sales-based financing (merchant cash advance), reported effective 31 Dec 2026.
citation: Venable (Mar 2026) via search; JD Supra. Verify each statute.

rule: Max 7(a) loan $5m. SBA guarantee up to **85%** for loans ≤ $150,000 and up to **75%** above $150,000. Max SBA-guaranteed exposure per borrower plus affiliates $3.75m.
citation: 13 CFR 120.210 (eCFR); SOP 50 10 8 (citing 13 CFR 120.151); SBA Policy Notice 5000-879058

rule: Single 504 debenture max $5.5m. From 4 Jul 2026, a borrower can hold a 7(a) up to $5m and 504 debentures up to $5m at the same time (combined $10m). The $3.75m guaranteed-exposure cap still applies to 7(a).
citation: SBA Policy Notice 5000-879058 (via NAGGL); Coleman Report

rule: SOP 50 10 8.1, published 14 Aug 2026, **effective 1 Oct 2026** for applications given an SBA loan number on/after that date. SOP 50 10 8.0 applies to applications up to 30 Sep 2026.
citation: SBA Information Notice 5000-880695

rule: SBA helps only applicants who cannot get the credit on reasonable terms from non-government sources. Lender certifies this by submitting the application and keeps supporting documents. Factors: industry, business age ≤ 2 years, collateral, term needed, etc. Lender must state the specific reasons.
citation: 13 CFR 120.101 (eCFR); SBA Procedural Notice 5000-875701

rule: Debt service coverage (operating cash flow / debt service) **≥ 1.15** on historical and/or projected basis, and **≥ 1:1 on a global basis**. Start-ups and projections: ≥ 1.15 within 2 years of funding.
citation: SOP 50 10 8.0 text. Verify unchanged in 8.1.

rule: SBSS score sunset. From 1 Mar 2026: 7(a) Small Loans need DSCR **≥ 1.1:1**. Credit scoring not required. Internal models allowed if they do not rely solely on consumer credit scores.
citation: SBA Procedural Notice 5000-875701 (pub. 16 Jan 2026, eff. 1 Mar 2026), via NAGGL

rule: Start-ups (operating ≤ 1 year): at least 10% of total project cost. Changes of ownership: 10% of price or 9:1 debt-to-worth test.
citation: SOP 50 10 8.0. 8.1 changed change-of-ownership rules (Appendix 15). Verify.

rule: Owners of **≥ 20%** generally must guarantee the loan. Lender may require others.

Loan must be "fully secured" as far as possible. If business assets fall short, the lender must take available equity in personal real estate of 20%+ owners and guarantors (home included), up to the shortfall. **Not required if equity is < 25% of market value.** A loan must not be declined only for lack of collateral. Haircuts: improved real estate 85%, new equipment 75%, trading assets 10%.
citation: SOP 50 10 8.0, Standard 7(a) collateral section. Verify in 8.1.

rule: A lender may not require the spouse's signature if the applicant qualifies alone. If a guarantor is needed, the lender may not require that it be the spouse.
citation: 12 CFR 1002.7(d)(1), (d)(5) (eCFR). Business scope: verify in the official interpretations.

rule: No SME support factor in current US rules. Corporate exposures 100% under the standardised approach. A Mar 2026 Basel III endgame reproposal would cut corporate to 95% (standardised) and 65% for investment-grade at the largest banks. Reportedly no special SME risk weight. **Proposal only, not final.**
citation: Covington; Arnold & Porter; Simpson Thacher (Mar–Apr 2026)

rule: Debt limit for Subchapter V is $3,424,000 for cases from 1 Apr 2025 (the temporary $7.5m limit ended in Jun 2024). Senate passed S. 3977 on 4 Aug 2026 to restore $7.5m. Not confirmed as law.
citation: ABI; California Lawyers Assn; Bernstein Shur (2026). Verify on Congress.gov.
